messages:
james_support: Escalation from ACME — their invoice-export flow regressed after the v2.2 rollout. They say a tiny template whitespace change now causes the model to return free-form text instead of the JSON blob our parser expects. Customer flagged as P1 (billing pipeline blocked). Attaching repro below.

james_support: Repro (customer provided):
```
# Template (worked before):
User: Generate a JSON invoice. Respond ONLY with valid JSON.
Template: "{{customer_name}}\n\nItems:\n- desc: Item A\n  price: 100\nTotal: $100"

# Template (after minor change): removed extra blank line between name and items ("\n\n" -> "\n")
Template: "{{customer_name}}\nItems:\n- desc: Item A\n  price: 100\nTotal: $100"

# API call (redacted):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-2.2","input":"<rendered template>","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":512,"stop":["\n\n"]}'

# Observed response: HTTP/200

Invoice total is $100. Thank you for your business.

(plain text, no JSON)
```

olivia_engineer: Can you paste the exact request body and the response body (raw)? Also which model alias did they hit? Is this only ACME or multiple customers? :eyes:

james_support: Pasted the raw body above — they hit the default alias (redwood-instruct -> v2.2). Seen at least two other customers in the same account complaining after yesterday's rollout.

kenji_oncall: Oncall triage: did we change any tokenizer/normalization or prompt-preprocessing in the rollout? I saw a PR about trimming duplicate newlines.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for alias redwood-instruct -> v2.2 at 2026-02-13T22:11:02Z; current canary 20% of traffic.

sre-bot: Metrics snapshot: pre-rollout JSON-parse errors ~0.8% (baseline). After canary jump -> 4.6% on v2.2 across customers using invoice templates. Median latency unchanged; tail latency +10% p99.

ai-ops: Quick theory: v2.2 updated instruction-following behavior to be more conversational when prompts are less strictly constrained. The small whitespace change may have shifted tokenization/context windows so model prefers a short human-like closing instead of strict JSON.

olivia_engineer: Good call. We should try 2 things: 1) repro locally with the exact rendered prompt and model params, 2) test forcing JSON-only with an explicit schema instruction or function-calling shim.

james_support: Customer tried adding a leading JSON schema line and it partially helped but they don't want to change templates across thousands of invoices. They want a rollback or routing fix.

maria_pm: ACME is an enterprise customer on a dedicated plan — this is impacting billing. They asked for ETA and whether we can pin them to previous behavior ASAP.

kenji_oncall: Actionable: rollback canary to v2.1 for the default alias OR introduce routing rule to send this customer's requests to pinned v2.1. Which is faster?

olivia_engineer: Routing rule is fastest (no code deploy). I can add an allowlist to route ACME org_id -> v2.1 alias within ~20 minutes. I'll also open a model-onboarding ticket to investigate prompt sensitivity in v2.2.

ai-ops: Repro steps I'm running now (local):
```
# reproduce (dev env)
echo '"{{customer_name}}\nItems:\n- desc: Item A\n  price: 100\nTotal: $100"' > example_prompt.txt
python -c "import requests,os; print(requests.post('https://dev.api.redwood/v1/generate', json={'model':'redwood-instruct-2.2','input':open('example_prompt.txt').read(),'temperature':0.0,'max_tokens':512}).text)"
```

ai-ops: Early result: v2.2 returns the plain-language closing ~60% of runs when stop token is only `\n\n`. v2.1 still returns strict JSON in our test.

olivia_engineer: Temporary mitigation: for customers with templated JSON responses, require `stop` that matches end-of-JSON (e.g., `"\n"` + `}`) or add explicit final token instruction: "Output ONLY valid JSON and end with `}`". We'll provide this as a supported best-practice and apply routing for ACME.

james_support: I told ACME we can route them to v2.1 immediately and provide a recommended prompt change for long term. They asked for a short-term rollback rather than template edits.

kenji_oncall: I'll coordinate with infra to apply routing rule and monitor customer traffic. Also start an incident with priority P1 and add Model Onboarding + Research.

deploy-bot: routing: rule created to route org:acme-corp -> alias redwood-instruct@v2.1 at 2026-02-13T23:04:11Z by olivia_engineer.

sre-bot: Post-routing metrics (5m): JSON-parse errors for ACME dropped back to baseline. Overall error rates still elevated for other customers on v2.2.

olivia_engineer: Next steps (owner: olivia_engineer):
- Keep ACME pinned to v2.1 until root cause identified.
- Run A/B with strict JSON enforcement prompts and function-calling to see if behavior stabilizes.
- Add regression tests for prompt-template whitespace variants in our onboarding harness.

james_support: I'll close the customer loop and offer the routing + recommended prompt patch. They accepted routing and will hold off on bulk edits. :thumbsup:

maria_pm: Please add timeline for a permanent fix to the incident. We need comms for other affected customers.

olivia_engineer: Will update incident ticket with timeline after first repro and root-cause. Expect initial RCA within 48 hours.

kenji_oncall: Noted. Flagging potential follow-ups: tokenizer normalization changes, system prompt tweaks, and instruction-following updates in v2.2 training/config.

james_support: Thanks team. I'll mark this thread P1 and keep updates here.
